aiBoxes.templateText:
Convert the raw property data below into a professional Facebook rental post for Myanmar customers in Bangkok.

FOLLOW THE OUTPUT STRUCTURE EXACTLY.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
MYANMAR HEADER — VERY IMPORTANT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The FIRST paragraph MUST be a natural, friendly, attractive Myanmar-language rental advertisement.

Do NOT make the header short or simply translate the project name and price.

When the information is available, the header should naturally combine:

- Rental price
- BTS/MRT station name
- BTS/MRT proximity or distance
- Condo/project name
- Floor
- Room size
- Bedroom type
- One attractive unit feature such as clean room, spacious room, high floor, nice view, new project, fully furnished, etc.

The header should feel like a Myanmar real estate agent naturally introducing the property on Facebook.

Use a conversational ending such as:
- ငှားဖို့ရှိပါတယ်ရှင့်
- ငှားရန်ရှိပါတယ်ရှင့်
- ငှားပေးနေပါတယ်ရှင့်
- အခန်းလေး ငှားဖို့ရှိပါတယ်နော်

Choose the wording naturally.

DO NOT use a fixed sentence every time.
Change the sentence structure naturally depending on the property.

GOOD EXAMPLE:

11,000 THB နဲ့ BTS Bangna ဘူတာအနီး Regent Home Bangna မှာ 25th Floor က 28 Sq.m. ကျယ်ဝန်းတဲ့ 1 Bedroom အခန်းသန့်လေး ငှားဖို့ရှိပါတယ်ရှင့်။

GOOD EXAMPLE:

BTS Bangna ဘူတာအနီး Regent Home Bangna ရဲ့ 25th Floor မှာ 28 Sq.m. ကျယ်တဲ့ 1 Bedroom အခန်းလေးကို 11,000 THB နဲ့ ငှားရန်ရှိပါတယ်ရှင့်။

GOOD EXAMPLE:

BTS Bangna ဘူတာနဲ့နီးတဲ့ Regent Home Bangna မှာ 11,000 THB နဲ့ 25th Floor က 28 Sq.m. 1 Bedroom အခန်းသန့်လေး ငှားဖို့ရှိပါတယ်ရှင့်။

GOOD EXAMPLE:

11,000 THB နဲ့ BTS Bangna အနီး Regent Home Bangna ရဲ့ 25th Floor မှာ 28 Sq.m. 1 Bedroom အခန်းလေး ငှားရန်ရှိပါတယ်ရှင့်။

IMPORTANT:
- The header should normally contain AT LEAST 4 useful property details when those details are available.
- PRIORITIZE price + BTS/MRT + project + size + floor + bedroom.
- If BTS/MRT information is available, include it.
- If BTS distance is available, include the actual distance.
- If only the station is available, use "BTS [Station] ဘူတာအနီး".
- If size is available, include Sq.m.
- If floor is available, include the floor.
- If bedroom type is available, include it.
- Add ONE useful descriptive phrase when supported by the raw data, such as "အခန်းသန့်လေး", "အခန်းကျယ်လေး", "အခန်းလှလေး", "High-Floor အခန်းလေး", or "View ကောင်းတဲ့အခန်းလေး".
- NEVER invent a descriptive feature. Only use it when supported by the raw data.
- Do NOT say the condo is "near BTS" unless the raw data actually gives BTS information.
- Do NOT use "Condo အနီး" as a substitute for BTS/location proximity.
- The header should be 1–2 natural sentences.
- Do NOT make it sound like a literal translation.
- Do NOT use Myanmar numerals.
- ALL numbers in the Myanmar header MUST use English numerals.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
ENGLISH PROPERTY TITLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Immediately after the Myanmar header:

[Project Name] | [Room Type] | [Size] | [Floor, Building] | [Price] THB

Example:

Regent Home Bangna | 1 Bedroom | 28 Sq.m. | 25th Floor, Building D | 11,000 THB

Rules:
- Use "1 Bedroom", "2 Bedroom", etc.
- Use "Sq.m."
- Use "25th Floor", "18th Floor", etc.
- Include Building when provided.
- Do NOT add "/month" to this title.
- Do NOT add information that is not available.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
PROPERTY OVERVIEW
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘁𝘆 𝗢𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄

Include the main property information from the raw data.

Example:

• 1 Bedroom | 1 Bathroom
• Size: 28 Sq.m.
• Building D | 25th Floor
• High-Floor Panoramic View
• New Project Development
• Fully Furnished & Fully Equipped
• Ready to Move In

Rules:
- Include useful details that actually exist.
- Do not invent information.
- Keep each bullet focused.
- Do not put a large amount of unrelated information into one bullet.
- Do not include agent/co-agent information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY HIGHLIGHTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀

Include important selling points that are supported by the raw data.

Examples:

• Near BTS Bangna Station
• High-Floor Unit
• New Project Development
• Panoramic View
• Ready to Move In

Do not simply copy every Property Overview bullet.
Use this section to highlight the property's useful advantages.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
FURNITURE & APPLIANCES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If furniture or appliances are mentioned:

𝗙𝘂𝗿𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 & 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲𝘀

List the actual items.

Example:

• 6-Foot Bed
• 180 cm Wardrobe
• 2 Air Conditioners (12,000 BTU each)
• Front-Load Washing Machine
• Samsung Refrigerator
• Microwave
• Water Heater

IMPORTANT:
- Do NOT summarize a detailed list as "necessary appliances".
- Keep quantities, brands, sizes, and capacities when provided.
- Do NOT invent appliances.
- Do not remove useful appliance information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
FACILITIES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If facilities are mentioned:

𝗙𝗮𝗰𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀

List the useful facilities.

Example:

• Swimming Pool
• Fully Equipped Gym
• Co-Working Space
• Children's Playground
• Keycard Access Control
• CCTV Monitoring
• 24-Hour Security

Do not invent facilities.
Do not list unnecessary minor facilities if there are many.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
LOCATION & TRANSIT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If location information exists:

𝗟𝗼𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗶𝘁

Example:

• Near BTS Bangna Station
• 600 meters to BTS Udomsuk
• Walking Distance to BTS
• Near Makro
• Easy Access to Sukhumvit Road
• Near BITEC Bangna

Use actual distances and locations from the raw data.
Do not invent nearby places.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
RENTAL TERMS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If rental conditions exist:

𝗥𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗧𝗲𝗿𝗺𝘀

Example:

• Rental Price: 11,000 THB/month
• Minimum 1-Year Contract
• 2 Months Security Deposit + 1 Month Advance Rent
• Ready to Move In

Only include conditions provided in the raw data.

REMOVE:
- Agents Welcome
- Co-Agent Friendly
- No Co-Agent
- Agent commission
- Owner/agent conditions
- Agent-to-agent information

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SERVICE FEE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ALWAYS include this exact line:

🔴 𝗦𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗙𝗲𝗲 လုံးဝမရှိပါဘူးရှင့် 🔴

If the raw data explicitly states a different service fee, replace this line with the actual service fee information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CONTACT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ALWAYS use exactly:

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗰𝘁 for Viewing
• Call / WhatsApp: 062-718-8699
• LINE: @sweetiehsu
• Property Code: BHV-XXXXX-XXXXX

Do NOT use the original phone number or LINE ID from the raw data.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
PROPERTY CODE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate a UNIQUE property code.

Format:

BHV-XXXXX-XXXXX

Rules:
- Must start with BHV-
- First section = exactly 5 uppercase letters/numbers
- Second section = exactly 5 uppercase letters/numbers
- Example: BHV-K7M2Q-X9P4L
- Generate a new unique code every time.
- Never copy an existing code from the raw data.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
HASHTAGS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate approximately 12–18 relevant English hashtags.

Use only information supported by the raw data.

Include relevant:
- Project
- Location
- BTS/MRT
- Condo
- Rental
- Bangkok
- Property features

Example:

#RegentHomeBangna #RegentHome #BTSBangna #NewProject #BangnaCondo #SukhumvitCondo #CondoForRent #RentCondoBangkok #BangkokCondo #BangkokRental #CondoNearBTS #HighFloorCondo #ThailandProperty #BangkokProperty #BangkokRealEstate #ReadyToMoveIn

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
REMOVE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Never include:
- Owner Post
- Agent Post
- Owner
- Agent
- Co-Agent
- Co-Agent Welcome
- Co-Agent Friendly
- No Co-Agent
- Commission
- Agent commission
- Agent-only information
- Original agent contact information

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
LANGUAGE & NUMBER RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

- Myanmar header only.
- Everything after the Myanmar header must be English.
- Use ENGLISH NUMERALS ONLY.
- Never use Myanmar numerals.
- Do NOT use emojis anywhere except the default Service Fee line.
- Keep project names and proper nouns in English.
- Keep BTS/MRT names in English.
- Keep THB, Sq.m., KG, BTU, etc. in English.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
FINAL OUTPUT ORDER
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

[FRIENDLY, DETAILED MYANMAR HEADER]

[Project Name] | [Room Type] | [Size] | [Floor, Building] | [Price] THB

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘁𝘆 𝗢𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄

aiBoxes.browserPromptText:
Edit the attached interior photograph into a clean, detailed, professional architectural real-estate image.
Use the original photograph as the source of truth. Preserve the real interior while correcting photographic defects.
MANDATORY RESULT
Perform BOTH:
1. Architectural straightening and geometric balance correction.
2. Restrained, realistic image-quality enhancement.
Sharpening alone is insufficient. Correct visible camera tilt and leaning architectural verticals.
PRIORITY ORDER
1. Preserve the actual room, objects, materials, proportions, and spatial relationships.
2. Correct camera roll, vertical convergence, and visible lens distortion.
3. Preserve the original lighting, colors, white balance, and atmosphere.
4. Improve clarity and technical quality.
5. Adapt the corrected photograph to the requested output format.
Original framing and perspective are references, not locks on camera defects. Small changes in crop and apparent object positions caused by legitimate geometric correction are permitted.
STEP 1 — ARCHITECTURAL STRAIGHTENING
Before enhancing detail, inspect the photograph for:
* Left or right camera tilt.
* Leaning architectural verticals.
* Vertical keystone convergence.
* Visible lens distortion.
* An uneven-looking floor or cabinet base caused by camera orientation.
Use reliable upright references such as:
* Wall corners.
* Wardrobe sides.
* Cabinet door seams.
* Doorframes.
* Window jambs.
Correct camera roll and vertical convergence so genuinely upright architectural edges appear straight and parallel to the image’s vertical axis.
Apply one coherent photographic perspective correction across the scene. Do not separately rotate, stretch, bend, or reposition individual objects.
Do not force every horizontal-looking line to become horizontal. Lines receding into depth must retain realistic perspective and consistent vanishing directions.
Keep the floor plane, furniture bases, and wall junctions geometrically consistent.
Preserve believable furniture proportions, natural asymmetry, and room depth.
Retain the original viewing direction and the same visible faces of furniture. Do not simulate a new camera location or invent a front-facing view.
The result must look upright and stable. Do not hide unresolved tilt merely by cropping.
STEP 2 — PRESERVE THE ACTUAL INTERIOR
Preserve every existing:
* Architectural feature.
* Wall, ceiling, floor, and opening.
* Furniture item and built-in element.
* Appliance and fixture.
* Handle, switch, socket, and fitting.
* Decoration, accessory, and small object.
* Plant.
* Visible exterior detail.
Keep their original physical locations, sizes, shapes, materials, colors, finishes, and relationships.
Apparent image-coordinate changes resulting from global perspective correction are allowed. Physical changes to the room are prohibited.
Do not redesign, stage, tidy, replace, duplicate, recolor, or reposition anything.
Do not remove small objects simply because they appear untidy.
Preserve existing plant types, shapes, sizes, positions, colors, and density.
STEP 3 — PRESERVE LIGHTING AND COLOR
Match the source photograph’s:
* Overall brightness.
* White balance and color temperature.
* Color palette and saturation.
* Lighting direction.
* Shadow placement and depth.
* Highlight relationships.
* Reflections.
* Mood and atmosphere.
Do not automatically brighten or warm the photograph to make it look luxurious.
Keep a warm room warm, a cool room cool, and a neutral room neutral.
Do not neutralize an authentic color cast or turn pale materials into pure white.
Recover highlights and shadow detail conservatively, only where supported by the source. Maintain natural differences between bright and dark areas.
No artificial sunlight, added illumination, switched-on lights, cinematic grading, HDR appearance, or dramatic relighting.
STEP 4 — RESTRAINED TECHNICAL RESTORATION
Improve:
* Fine edge definition.
* Supported texture detail.
* Clarity.
* Compression quality.
* Mild softness.
* Digital and color noise.
Preserve natural detail in wood, fabric, upholstery, glass, metal, stone, walls, and flooring.
Use conservative sharpening and noise reduction.
Avoid halos, crunchy edges, plastic surfaces, excessive smoothing, exaggerated contrast, and synthetic textures.
Do not invent wood grain, labels, patterns, or detail absent from the source. Keep genuinely unresolved details natural.
Preserve realistic depth of field.
STEP 5 — HUMAN PRESENCE
If people, body parts, photographer reflections, camera reflections, or tripod reflections are visible, remove only those elements.
Reconstruct only the immediately obscured background conservatively.
Preserve unrelated objects, natural reflections, lighting, and architectural shadows.
If no human or camera presence exists, make no removal edits.
STEP 6 — FRAMING AND OUTPUT
Target:
* 1080 × 1350 pixels.
* 4:5 vertical format.
* sRGB.
* High-quality output suitable for Facebook Feed, Instagram Feed, and real-estate listings.
Complete perspective correction before final framing.
Use the smallest practical crop. Preserve important furniture, openings, décor, and architectural features.
When trimming is necessary, prioritize unimportant blank ceiling or floor.
Do not stretch the image to fit the aspect ratio.
Do not expand the room or invent unseen architecture.
If 4:5 framing would remove essential content, preserve the corrected photograph and use a plain unobtrusive border instead of fabricated scenery.
If exact pixel export is unavailable, produce the highest supported resolution in the correct 4:5 ratio.
STEP 7 — FINAL VERIFICATION
Compare the finished image against the original.
Confirm:
* Visible camera roll is corrected.
* Upright architectural edges are straight.
* Receding lines retain natural perspective.
* The floor and furniture bases remain geometrically consistent.
* Furniture and room proportions remain believable.
* Existing objects and small details remain present.
* Colors, brightness, lighting, and atmosphere remain faithful.
* Texture enhancement remains natural.
* No important elements are unnecessarily cropped.
STRICT NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS
No:
* Interior redesign or virtual staging.
* Added, replaced, duplicated, or repositioned objects.
* Changed materials or colors.
* Artificial symmetry.
* New camera viewpoint.
* Warped walls or furniture.
* Stretched room proportions.
* Invented architectural details.
* Fabricated textures.
* Artificial sunlight or shadows.
* Excessive brightness or warmth.
* HDR or cinematic grading.
* CGI appearance.
* Oversharpening or excessive smoothing.
* Text, graphics, borders unless required above, logos, or watermarks.
Return ONE finished photograph with visibly corrected architectural alignment and restrained technical enhancement, faithfully preserving the original interior.
